urn:li:share:7452969504843788288.article_title: How to evaluate the performance of AI agents?
urn:li:share:7452969504843788288.comment_text:
Nobody tells you how to know if your AI agent is actually working.

Building an agent is the easy part. Knowing whether it's doing the right thing — that's where most teams are flying blind. 🎯 You can run it in a sandbox with fixed inputs and check the outputs automatically (offline), or watch it live in production and catch drift before it becomes a crisis (online).

Testing an agent is like tasting soup while you cook, not just before you serve it.
Are you doing any structured evaluation before shipping agents to real users?
#AI #SoftwareEngineering #AIAgents

urn:li:share:7453146318094516224.article_title: Shopify's AI Phase Transition: Unlimited Opus-4.6 Token Budget
urn:li:share:7453146318094516224.comment_text:
Shopify gave their AI an unlimited thinking budget. Here's what happened.

Shopify's CTO just went on record about running Claude Opus with no token cap — meaning the model can "think" for as long as it needs before answering, like a consultant who actually reads the whole brief before speaking. 🧠 They're not treating AI as a feature. They're rebuilding how the company works around it, and they have the internal adoption numbers to back it up.

Most teams limit AI to save cost. Shopify bet that removing that ceiling changes the quality of output entirely — and so far, the data says they're right.
Are you capping your AI's reasoning budget, and have you actually measured what that costs you in output quality?
#AI #Shopify #SoftwareEngineering

urn:li:share:7454822463219363841.article_title: An open-source spec for orchestration: Symphony
urn:li:share:7454822463219363841.comment_text:
Your issue tracker is now an agent's to-do list

OpenAI dropped Symphony, an open-source spec that wires Codex directly into orchestration pipelines — so agents pick up tickets, write code, and ship without waiting for a human to context-switch back 🔄 It's not a product, it's a contract between your tools and your agents, which means any team can build on top of it.

TAKEAWAY: Symphony is to agent workflows what REST was to APIs — a shared language that stops everyone from reinventing the plumbing.
QUESTION: If agents start triaging and closing issues autonomously, which part of your current review process becomes the bottleneck first?
#softwaredevelopment #agentic #openai

urn:li:share:7457377470116315136.article_title: The Claude Code system that replaces a 5-person team

urn:li:share:7463996471172870145.article_title: Amazon Q Developer agentic capabilities on SWE-Bench
urn:li:share:7463996471172870145.comment_text:
Amazon Q just topped the SWE-Bench leaderboard.

SWE-Bench isn't a toy benchmark — it throws real GitHub issues at an agent and expects working code across multiple files, no hand-holding. Amazon Q Developer resolved more of them end-to-end than any other system tested. 🧩 That means reading the issue, navigating an unfamiliar codebase, making the right changes, and passing the tests.

Benchmarks are like a driving test: passing it doesn't make you a good driver, but failing it tells you something real.
If an agent handled your last three bug tickets autonomously, which one would have quietly introduced a regression?
#SoftwareEngineering #AIAgents #AmazonQ

urn:li:share:7464021245605457920.article_title: Giving Agents Computers — Ivan Burazin, Daytona
urn:li:share:7464021245605457920.comment_text:
850,000 agent sandbox executions. Per day.

The infrastructure layer for AI agents is maturing faster than most enterprise roadmaps anticipated — and it's not happening inside hyperscaler clouds, it's happening on bare metal built specifically for ephemeral, code-executing agents. 🖥️ The implication is concrete: if your agents can't spin up isolated, reproducible environments in milliseconds, you're not bottlenecked by the model — you're bottlenecked by the ground it runs on. In every architecture review I run right now, this is the gap nobody budgeted for.

The model is the easy part. The execution environment is where enterprise AI either scales or stalls.
When your agents start writing and running code autonomously, which part of your current infrastructure stack becomes the ceiling?
#EnterpriseAI #AIArchitecture #AIStrategy

urn:li:share:7472649368299372544.article_title: [AINews] Satya on Loopcraft: Building Frontier Ecosystems
urn:li:share:7472649368299372544.comment_text:
Satya's essay isn't about products. It's about control.

Nadella just published a framing — 'Loopcraft' — that positions Microsoft's stack as the default architecture for how frontier AI ecosystems get built. 🏗️ For enterprises, this matters less as a tech choice and more as a procurement and dependency decision that will be very hard to reverse once agents start talking to agents inside your infrastructure. The vendor who defines the loop owns the leverage — and most enterprises are signing up without realizing it.

urn:li:share:7474813534628007937.article_title: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 60-95% fewer tokens, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server. - headroomlabs-ai/headroom
urn:li:share:7474813534628007937.comment_text:
Your AI infrastructure bill is a context problem.

As enterprises move from single-model calls to agentic pipelines — tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, file contents all stacking up — the context window becomes a cost center, not just a technical constraint. 🧮 A workflow that retrieves 10 documents, runs 5 tools, and loops three times can easily burn 10x the tokens you budgeted for. In every architecture review I run, token economics is the line item that surprises leadership the most, and it's almost never in the original business case.

The real AI cost conversation isn't about model pricing — it's about what you're feeding the model before it even starts thinking.
If you scaled your current AI workflows 100x tomorrow, do you know where your token spend would break your unit economics first?
#EnterpriseAI #AIArchitecture #AIStrategy
